description:
MaterialState has no minor-actinide inventory, but several ported correlations
want one:

- thermalExpansionMatproUPuO2 and the Lemehov UPuO2 model discount the plutonium
  fraction by americium and neptunium number densities.
- Lemehov's melting-point correlation has an explicit Am term.
- conductivityKatoMox and conductivityMagniMamox currently carry Am/Np as variant
  payload precisely because MaterialState cannot express them.

The port assumes zero minor actinides and documents that this over-predicts the
melting point (and so under-predicts strain) for MA-bearing fuel.

If MA-MOX is in scope, add am_fraction and np_fraction to MaterialState and move
the Kato/MAMOX payloads onto it. If it is not in scope, close this and keep the
documented assumption.
title: offbeat: decide whether MaterialState needs minor-actinide (Am/Np) fractions for MA-MOX fuel

description: Found 2026-08-11 by read-only correlation audit during op-4542 (Wakao) fix. In crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/heat_transfer_correlations/nusselt_number_correlations/enums.rs, fn estimate_based_on_prandtl_reynolds_and_wall_correction, the PipeGnielinskiCalibrated arm (~L462-471 at audit time) assigns modified_data.prandtl_wall = bulk_prandtl_number_input and modified_data.prandtl_bulk = wall_prandtl_number_input -- transposed relative to every other arm in the same function and to the sibling fn estimate_based_on_prandtl_darcy_and_reynolds_wall_correction, which handles the same variant correctly. Effect: Nu evaluated at Pr_wall instead of Pr_bulk and the Gnielinski (Pr_bulk/Pr_wall)^0.11 wall correction inverted. LATENT: audit traced all production preprocessing call sites (shell-and-tube, porous media, insulated pipes, clamshell heater) to the correct darcy variant, so CIET calibrated regressions are not currently corrupted; the buggy arm is reachable only by direct calls. Same error class as the Wakao Re/Pr transposition (op-4542).
title: tuas: PipeGnielinskiCalibrated wall-correction arm swaps Pr_bulk and Pr_wall

notes.author: teddy0@arch-desktop-aftershock
notes.content:
ComputeType backend selector landed (agent session 2026-07-17, worktree agent-aef7997cc5bb1753f). New src/physics/compute.rs: enum ComputeType { CpuSingleThread (default, trusted f64 reference), CpuMultiThread(ThreadCount), Gpu } + ThreadCount { Auto/Fixed/Fraction } with resolve(). Wired into KeffSettings.compute + run_keff dispatcher -> run_keff_cpu_single / run_keff_cpu_multi / run_keff_gpu. 

CpuMultiThread: dedicated rayon pool sized by ThreadCount::resolve() (Auto = available_parallelism; 12 cores here), per-history LCG jump-ahead seeds -> reproducible independent of thread count (verified bit-for-bit). Measured ~7.4x speedup (2.44s -> 0.33s, 20k histories x 80 gen).

Gpu: GENUINE partial wire-in of the op-u6s.3/union_grid GPU kernel into the eigenvalue loop -- each generation batches all source birth-energy Sigma_t through UnionTotalXs::lookup_gpu (f32, RTX 3050) as first-flight XS; subsequent collisions use the same table on CPU. Graceful CPU fallback (never errors; Android cfg'd to CPU). NO GPU speedup on this homogeneous case (2.66s, kernel-launch bound; branchy walk stays CPU) -- honest, documented. 

3-mode k agreement (RTX 3050, real): single 1.00762+/-0.00827, multi 1.00715+/-0.00768, gpu 1.00066+/-0.00839; single-vs-gpu 0.59 sigma. 80 lib tests pass (78 baseline + 2 new), android-clean, clippy-clean. UNTRUSTED AI DRAFT manifest: crates/outram-mc-libs/docs/ai-fleet-review/compute-type/REVIEW_MANIFEST.md.

REMAINING for op-u6s.4 (kept open): (a) native-breakpoint union grid (still a dense log resample); (b) deeper GPU penetration than first-flight-only (event-based collision-site batch); (c) honour ComputeType in the CSG/MG/delta drivers (currently only run_keff dispatches).

title: outram-mc: wire GPU batched XS interpolation into a real transport sweep / unionized sigma(E) table
